summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen led Joe Goss for seven rounds near Walton, Ky., until militia broke up the fight; it resumed in Boone County, Goss won on a foul in the 21st round and Allen was arrested at Newport.

metadata.notes: Page masthead reads 'The St. Louis Republican, Friday Morning, September 8, 1876', page 5. Dispatches dated Sept. 7. Filed under Missouri Republican per the rubric.

facts.fact: Allen and Joe Goss fought near Walton, Ky., on the Louisville Short Line 18 miles from Cincinnati, starting at 7:35 a.m.; the Covington Light Guard militia stopped it at the seventh round with Allen ahead

The fight resumed in a second ring a short distance below Walton in Boone County; Goss won on a foul in the 21st round when Allen struck him while he was on his knees, at 11:50 a.m., after 1 hour 52 minutes
Allen was arrested when the trains from the fight arrived at Newport, Ky.
Allen and Goss stayed at the Gibson House in Cincinnati the night before the fight; Allen's seconds were Tom Kelly and Arthur Chambers
Allen came from a fighting family in Birmingham, England, and learned gun-making as a youth
Allen served in the army in the Crimean War and won several 'turn-ups' in front of Sevastopol, which convinced him he could be a champion
Allen beat Jack Gould for 15 pounds a side in 51 rounds, 1 hour 22 minutes
Allen lost to Bob Smith, an American Black fighter, after 108 rounds lasting 3 hours 57 minutes, for 5 pounds a side
Allen beat George Iles for 100 pounds a side in 15 rounds, 52 minutes
Allen fought Joe Goss in England for 100 pounds a side; the fight lasted until night and was declared a draw
Goss then matched himself with Allen's brother Harry for 100 pounds a side, but police arrested Harry and the fight never took place
Allen came to America with featherweight Peter Morris, arriving in 1867
Allen's first fight in America was with Bill Davis for $1,000 a side, won by Allen in 40 rounds, 40 minutes
Charley Gallagher of Cleveland knocked Allen out in two rounds, three minutes, for $1,000 a side
Allen and Mike McCoole fought for $1,000; Allen had the best of it, but the crowd cut the ring and the fight was drawn after seven rounds
Allen beat Charley Gallagher in a rematch for $1,000 a side in 17 rounds, 22 minutes
Jem Mace beat Allen near New Orleans for $1,500 a side in 10 rounds, 44 minutes
Allen beat Jim Gallagher for $500 a side in 15 rounds, 22 minutes
Mike McCoole forfeited $1,000 on a match with Allen
Allen beat Mike McCoole near St. Louis in eight rounds, 19 minutes, in a match for $2,500
Allen beat Ben Hogan for $1,000 a side in three rounds, six minutes
George Rooke of Newark matched himself with Allen for $1,500 a side but did not appear; the stakes were drawn

notes: Headline says Goss won 'at the Twenty-Third Round' but the round-by-round AP report gives the foul in the 21st. 'Record of the Men' is reprinted from the Cincinnati Enquirer, so career facts are medium confidence; minor early English fights (Jack White, Morris Conner, Hall, Posh Price twice, 'Bingy' Rose, Jack Parkison) were left out.
